Stuck? Find your role below, then the situation that sounds like yours.
Every situation in the simulation has a move available — these are the
common ones.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Senators

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### I don't think I have anything to do.

There is always something moving. In rough priority order: check whether
either of your bills is on an upcoming agenda ([Committees](committees.qmd));
read the bills coming before *your* committee and decide your questions and
your vote; check your bill's letters — if a lobby filed "Oppose Unless
Amended," talk to them about what amendment would flip them; and talk to the
press. A senator nobody hears from doesn't get covered, and coverage is
influence.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### My bill is on the agenda in the next policy committee.

Prepare to present it: a two-minute statement of the problem, what the bill
does, and who supports it. Expect questions from members — read your own
bill's weak points first. Count your votes before the meeting, not during
it: talk to committee members, and look at what the lobbies filed on your
bill ([your bill's page](bills.qmd) shows every letter). If you don't have
the votes, an amendment before the hearing may be cheaper than a loss in it.
:::

## Lobbyists

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### I don't think I have anything to do.

Read the [dockets](committees.qmd) — every bill awaiting a hearing is a bill
you could be shaping. File positions on bills that touch your organization's
interests ([file a letter](lobby.qmd)); meet the authors of bills you want
amended; check which senators are up for contributions you haven't made yet;
and pitch story angles to journalists. Money and letters left unspent at the
end of the semester bought nothing.
:::

## Journalists

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### I don't think I have anything to do.

Scan the [Monitor](index.qmd): every recent vote, letter, and contribution
is a potential story. Who voted against their party? Which lobby is
spending big on one senator? Which bill died quietly? Post short items to
the Wire as things happen, and save the best thread for your outlet's next
full write-up.
:::

## Chairs & Leadership

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### I need to change my agenda at the last minute.

Just file the agenda form again for the same meeting date — the new
submission becomes the current agenda automatically (marked as a revision),
and the site shows only the newest version. Announce the change in class;
the site's copy is always the authoritative one.
:::

:::

Every official action happens through a form — they all live in
[**The Filing Cabinet**](forms.qmd).
